title: Imports and Dependencies
content: Imports $\texttt{Nat.Prime}$, $\texttt{ZMod}$, $\texttt{Finset.Card}$, $\texttt{Real}$, and $\texttt{Tactic}$ from Mathlib. The formalization works in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ for modular arithmetic and uses $\texttt{Finset}$ for the finite factorial residue set.
mathContext: Working in $\texttt{ZMod p}$ allows direct computation of $k! \bmod p$ as elements of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. The $\texttt{Finset.Card}$ library provides $|A_p|$.

title: Factorial Residue Set $A_p$
content: The set $A_p = \{k! \bmod p : 1 \leq k < p\}$ formalized as a $\texttt{Finset}$ over $\texttt{ZMod p}$ by mapping $k \mapsto (k+1)!$ for $k \in \{0, \ldots, p-2\}$. This gives all factorial residues from $1!$ through $(p-1)!$. The image operation automatically removes duplicates, so $|A_p| \leq p - 1$.

title: Factorial Residue Count
content: $\texttt{factorialResidueCount}(p) = |A_p|$, the number of distinct factorial residues modulo $p$. The conjecture predicts $|A_p| \sim (1 - 1/e) \cdot p \approx 0.6321p$. Known values: $|A_5| = 3$, $|A_7| = 4$, $|A_{11}| = 8$, $|A_{13}| = 9$.

title: Conjectured Density $1 - 1/e$
content: The conjectured asymptotic density $1 - e^{-1} \approx 0.63212$ arises from the birthday-problem heuristic: if each $k!$ independently landed on a uniform random residue, the expected coverage after $p-1$ steps would be $p \cdot (1 - (1-1/p)^{p-1}) \to p(1-1/e)$.
mathContext: $\texttt{conjecturedDensity} = 1 - e^{-1}$. From the coupon collector model: $\mathbb{E}[\text{coverage}] = n(1 - (1-1/n)^n) \to n(1-1/e)$.

title: Wilson's Theorem for Factorial Residues
content: Wilson's theorem states $(p-1)! \equiv -1 \pmod{p}$ for prime $p$. This means the last factorial in the sequence is $-1 \equiv p-1$, so $p-1 \in A_p$ always. Combined with $0 \notin A_p$, this gives $A_p \subseteq \{1, \ldots, p-1\}$.
mathContext: $(p-1)! \equiv -1 \pmod{p}$ (Wilson). So $A_p \ni p-1$ and $0 \notin A_p$, giving $|A_p| \leq p-1$.

title: Factorial Residues Exclude Zero
content: For primes $p > 2$, no $k!$ with $1 \leq k < p$ is divisible by $p$, since all factors $1, 2, \ldots, k$ are strictly less than $p$. Hence $0 \notin A_p$ and $A_p \subseteq (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^*$.
mathContext: $k < p \Rightarrow p \nmid k! \Rightarrow k! \not\equiv 0 \pmod{p}$. So $A_p \subseteq \{1, \ldots, p-1\}$.

title: Upper Bound $|A_p| \leq p - 2$
content: For $p > 5$, the factorial residue set satisfies $|A_p| \leq p - 2$: not all nonzero residues are hit. This is because factorial residues concentrate among smooth numbers (those with small prime factors), so residues that are primitive roots tend to be missed.

title: Ratio Set Covers $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^*$
content: The ratio set $A_p / A_p$ covers all nonzero residues: for any $r \neq 0$, there exist $a, b \in A_p$ with $a/b = r$. This follows because $(k+1)!/k! = k+1$ ranges over $\{2, \ldots, p-1\}$, and $1!/1! = 1$, covering all of $\{1, \ldots, p-1\}$.
mathContext: $A_p / A_p \supseteq \{1, 2, \ldots, p-1\} = (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^*$. Since $|A_p/A_p| \leq |A_p|^2$, this forces $|A_p|^2 \geq p - 1$.

title: Square-Root Lower Bound
content: The counting argument $|A_p/A_p| \leq |A_p|^2$ combined with $|A_p/A_p| \geq p - 1$ gives $|A_p| \geq \sqrt{p-1}$. This is the basic unconditional lower bound, far from the conjectured linear growth $\sim 0.63p$.

title: GSSV Improved Bound (2024)
content: Grebennikov, Sagdeev, Semchankau, and Vasilevskii (2024) improved the lower bound to $|A_p| \geq (\sqrt{2} - o(1))\sqrt{p}$ by proving $|A_p \cdot A_p| = (1+o(1))p$. Their product-set estimate exploits the multiplicative random walk structure of factorial residues.

title: Main Conjecture: $|A_p| \sim (1 - 1/e) \cdot p$
content: The central open problem: $|A_p|/p \to 1 - 1/e \approx 0.6321$ as $p \to \infty$ through primes. The gap between the best lower bound ($\sqrt{p}$ scale) and the conjectured truth (linear in $p$) is enormous—bridging $p^{1/2}$ to $p^1$ would require fundamentally new techniques.
mathContext: $\forall \varepsilon > 0,\; \exists P_0 : |\frac{|A_p|}{p} - (1 - e^{-1})| < \varepsilon$ for $p > P_0$ prime. Status: OPEN.

title: Birthday-Type Random Model
content: The heuristic: if each $k! \bmod p$ independently hit a uniformly random residue, the expected coverage after $p-1$ steps would be $p \cdot (1 - (1-1/p)^{p-1}) \to p(1 - 1/e)$. This is the classical birthday/coupon-collector argument. The axiom formalizes that $(1 - 1/p)^{p-1} \to e^{-1}$.
mathContext: $(1 - 1/p)^{p-1} \to e^{-1}$ as $p \to \infty$. Expected distinct values after $n$ uniform draws from $\{1,\ldots,n\}$: $n(1-(1-1/n)^n) \to n(1-1/e)$.

title: Factorial as Multiplicative Walk
content: The recursion $(k+1)! = (k+1) \cdot k!$ shows that the factorial sequence modulo $p$ is a multiplicative random walk on $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^*$: each step multiplies by $k+1$. Since $k+1$ ranges over $\{2, \ldots, p-1\}$, the multipliers are all distinct nonzero residues.
mathContext: $(k+1)! \equiv (k+1) \cdot k! \pmod{p}$. The sequence $1!, 2!, \ldots, (p-1)!$ is a walk on $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^*$ with step $k \mapsto k \cdot (k+1)$.

title: Klurman–Munsch Average Result (2017)
content: Oleksiy Klurman and Marc Munsch (2017) proved that the conjecture holds on average over primes: $\frac{\sum_{p \leq x} |A_p|}{\sum_{p \leq x} p} \to 1 - 1/e$. This confirms the random model prediction in an averaged sense, providing strong evidence for the pointwise conjecture.
mathContext: $\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{\sum_{p \leq x, p \text{ prime}} |A_p|}{\sum_{p \leq x, p \text{ prime}} p} = 1 - e^{-1}$ [Klurman–Munsch 2017].
